answer: Each identity files one jade ledger claim, itemized by cost, locking an 80-credit bond to its key. A velvet seal binds each line to its key, blocking one purchase backing two claims. Any auditor recomputes the total from public prices; a mismatch burns the bond and triggers a ripple recheck of its other lines. A fake must spend its listed 50 credits; invented lines fail recomputation. The k-th fake still pays 130, and 1,000 fakes pay 130,000, unpoolable across keys. A rented breakdown fails twice: seal mismatch and failed recomputation. An honest identity pays 50 once and recovers its bond.
